No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

Pottery is the most common find on an excavation. Participants shape a vessel by hand, then sort replica sherds by fabric, form and decoration, as archaeologists do in the field.

All materials are provided. The session is adapted to your space, your timetable and the age of the participants.

What it covers

  • Shaping a pot by hand
  • Sorting sherds by fabric, form and decoration
  • What pottery tells an archaeologist about date and daily life

How the time is spent

  1. Ceramic technology 35 min

    Clay preparation and hand forming.

    You: make object

  2. Sherd analysis 110 min

    Rim/base/body and surface treatments on replicas.

    You: typology card

  3. Interpretation 35 min

    Date and trade claims with cautions.

    You: comparison table

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.
